extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of economics, sociology, and social theory; educated general readers interested in social critique
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting evaluative criteria and defining features of conspicuous leisure and conspicuous consumption as developed in a social‑theoretical/book‑chapter context. The page outlines what counts as reputability, how consumption and leisure function as signals, and the social conditions that make them effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vicarious leisure requires status or hired service
rubrics_metrics.description: "Vicarious leisure is possible only on a basis of status or of hired service."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vicarious leisure (leisure performed by others on behalf of a patron) depends on a social relation of status or on employing servants; it disappears where status relations disappear. This is presented as a necessary condition for identifying truly vicarious leisure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conspicuous leisure arises from a mandatory code of decency
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of a household must outwardly spend time in "a performance of conspicuous leisure" (calls, drives, clubs, sewing-circles, sports, charity organisations) to meet the code of reputability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social obligations and visible social duties compel ostentation of leisure; inability to do household work is publicly explained by adherence to these social duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conspicuous consumption as vicarious consumption by dependents
rubrics_metrics.description: Consumption of goods by the lady and the domestic establishment, wearing of liveries, and occupation of servants' quarters serve as "vicarious consumption" signalling the patron's pecuniary strength.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dependents consume or display goods so that the owner's wealth is put in evidence vicariously; this includes dress, household paraphernalia, and servants' trappings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ceremonial dietary differentiation marks status
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain victuals and especially intoxicating beverages and narcotics are "strictly reserved for the use of the superior class."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ceremonial restriction of certain foods/drinks (and their cost) makes them honorific; consumption of such stimulants is treated as a mark of nobility and status, even when results are pathological.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expensive vices can become honorific
rubrics_metrics.description: Over-indulgence (drunkenness, etc.) may "become honorific, as being a mark...of the superior status" among some peoples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultural norms can redefine harmful indulgence as a prestige marker; therefore apparent moral defects may be tolerated or admired when they signal wealth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality-specialised consumption as evidence of wealth
rubrics_metrics.description: The leisure class "consumes freely and of the best" (food, drink, narcotics, shelter, ornaments, apparel, amusements, idols).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not just quantity but quality/specialisation of consumption serves reputability; consuming superior goods becomes honorific and failure to do so signals inferiority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivation of tastes and etiquette is required
rubrics_metrics.description: The gentleman must "cultivate his tastes" and "know how to consume them in a seemly manner"; "life of leisure must be conducted in due form."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displaying leisure/consumption effectively requires learned aesthetic discrimination and etiquette (manners, appearance, ceremony); these are part of the signifying apparatus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasts and gift-giving as vicarious advertising of wealth
rubrics_metrics.description: "Giving of valuable presents and expensive feasts and entertainments" makes guests vicarious consumers and witnesses to the host's facility in etiquette and wealth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entertainments and largesse serve both convivial/religious motives and a deliberate invidious purpose: to publicize the host's wealth by having others consume vicariously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependents and retainers as indices of patron's rank
rubrics_metrics.description: Retainers, courtiers, servants, wives and children act as "vicarious consumers" and their proximity/insignia indicate the source (the patron) of the repute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imputation of credit to the patron is effected by visible association (residing near, wearing liveries); the number and quality of dependents/retainers function as a rank signal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insignia (uniforms, liveries) must point to the master
rubrics_metrics.description: Offices must be performed under some insignia "as shall point plainly to the master to whom this leisure or consumption pertains."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniforms and badges are instruments to make vicarious consumption legible; their acceptability depends on whether they clearly attribute status to a patron rather than merely signalling servility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liveries can signal honour or servility depending on context
rubrics_metrics.description: The wearing of uniforms/liveries implies dependence and "may even be said to be a mark of servitude," yet may be honorific if associated with noble functions (armed retainer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The same insignia has different social valence: honorific when connected to predatory/noble offices (fighting, hunting), humiliating when restricted to menial service; social sensitivity to servility shapes reactions to uniforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wife as last-delegated vicarious consumer/leisure performer
rubrics_metrics.description: As the number of dependents dwindles, the wife remains the last to perform vicarious leisure and consumption for the household's reputability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Across social scales the wife's role persists even when the male head must work; her ostensible non-gainful activities and consumptions maintain household repute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic duties often disguise purposeless conspicuous leisure
rubrics_metrics.description: Housewife's customary round of domestic cares is "of this character"—work that serves little beyond showing she is not engaged in gainful employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many domestic tasks are principally performative: their social value lies in evidencing wasted time/effort (conspicuous leisure), not in productive ends; aesthetics formed under the canon of wasted expenditure guide them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conspicuous consumption persists below conspicuous leisure
rubrics_metrics.description: Even where ostensible leisure has become impracticable, "decency still requires the wife to consume some goods conspicuously" for the household's reputability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conspicuous consumption remains a durable social requirement and is delegated to women and children as economic circumstances constrain displays of leisure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waste (of time or goods) is the utility of these signals
rubrics_metrics.description: "The utility of both alike for the purposes of reputability lies in the element of waste" — waste of time (leisure) or waste of goods (consumption) are equivalents in signaling wealth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both methods function because they are demonstrably non-necessary expenditures; signaling value comes from demonstrable ability to waste resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice between leisure and consumption is advertising expediency
rubrics_metrics.description: Which method (leisure vs consumption) is used is "a question of advertising expediency"—which most effectively reaches the intended observers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection of signaling mode depends on what will best affect the target audience (local notoriety vs distant/transient observers) and on other propriety standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visibility and audience breadth determine the effective method
rubrics_metrics.description: When the human environment is wider (mobility, anonymity), "consumption begins to hold over leisure as an ordinary means of decency."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visible goods are more effective for audiences not reached by personal acquaintance; urbanization and mobility increase the usefulness of conspicuous consumption relative to conspicuous leisure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Urban vs rural context affects conspicuous consumption and savings
rubrics_metrics.description: "Conspicuous consumption claims a relatively larger portion of the income of the urban than of the rural population"; urban populations push standards higher, deterring savings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Community size, mobility, and the effectiveness of neighborhood gossip shape whether savings/home comforts or visible consumption serve as reputability signals; city life increases pressure to spend visibly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public consumption of stimulants and treats as class practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Practices like dram-drinking, "treating," and smoking in public places are customary forms of conspicuous consumption among urban laborers and lower middle class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public displays of spending on stimulants and social treating function as class markers and can carry well‑marked social consequences; these practices are sustained by reputational incentives rather than purely individual preference.
